steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line 24 muffin cups with paper liners.
Cream sugar and 1/2 cup butter in the bowl of a stand mixer until fluffy. Beat in eggs, one at a time, and mix 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla into mixture with the second egg.
Beat in flour and baking powder until thoroughly combined; beat in milk, lemon juice, and lemon zest to make a smooth batter.
Spoon batter into the prepared muffin cups.
Bake in the preheated oven until cupcake edges are slightly golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center of a cupcake comes out clean, 20 to 25 minutes. Cool cupcakes completely.

To make frosting: Beat 1 cup butter with 1 teaspoon vanilla and salt until smooth and creamy. Beat in confectioners' sugar, 1 cup at a time, to make a creamy frosting. Beat in blackberry jam. Spread frosting on cooled cupcakes.

raw_recipe.headline: Lemon Cupcake with Blackberry Buttercream
raw_recipe.description: Simple made-from-scratch lemon cupcakes with blackberry buttercream frosting. These treats are a refreshing hit with bright, tart, and sweet flavors.

video.description: These are cute, simple, and fancy cupcakes! Excellent for a party or just because you're craving a yummy flavor explosion.

review.reviewBody: Hi everyone! This is my recipe. Because it's kitchen tested I think the yield may have been modified- my original submission was for mini cupcakes, and I always use a piping bag and tip for frosting (which makes them mile-high, but no one ever seems to complain about it if you catch my drift)! That said, you should carefully watch larger cakes in your oven as this is the time I use for miniature cakes. If the batter seems way too dense, add a bit more milk to your liking, and always remember to use a stand or hand mixer. Enjoy!

Make sure ingredients are room temperature. This insured the mixture was not crumbly. I measured lemon juice to help be more consistent each time. I used 2 small to medium lemons, equaled 1/4 cup lemon juice. I used a heaping Tablespoon of batter in mini muffin pans. This made 30 cupcakes. Baked for 16-17 minutes. Next time I plan on using more lemon! These were light and not too dense.

I have had this recipe saved for years, wanting to try it--so I FINALLY got my act together and made the darn cupcakes! And I'm so glad I did! They are wonderful, and so incredibly beautiful!! The first time I tried the cupcake recipe as written, however, my cupcakes fell in the center. The second time, I made some adjustments and had better luck. I added 3/4 salt and 2 heaped tbsps of lemon zest (just for flavor), used half milk and half sour cream, and reduced the baking powder to 1 1/2 tsps. This worked much better for me, and gave me perfectly formed cupcakes. For the frosting, I had a stroke of luck at the grocery store and found a bag of freeze-dried blackberries (of all things!!), so I ground those up; sifted out the seeds; and added the powdered berries to the frosting (alongside all the other ingredients). I also added a good squeeze of lemon juice and some heavy cream to make up for the additional dry ingredients. The berry powder combined with the jam made for not only an absolutely gorgeous frosting, but also a very blackberry-forward one as well. The frosting complemented the cupcakes extremely well, and I am so pleased at the outcome. These cupcakes are a definite showstopper! I will definitely make them again (with my slight tweaks)! Thank you for sharing your recipe!

These were a hit! Made some modifications based on reviews. I doubled the cupcake recipe as I wanted 20+ standard sized cupcakes. They took about 25 minutes to bake in my oven at same temp recommended in the recipe. I did a single batch of the icing and on recommendation of a previous review, I used half butter and half shortening as I don’t care for a strong butter flavor. I also cut down to only 3 cups of confectioners sugar. The icing was plenty sweet and the consistency was just fine for piping on. Cupcakes were dense, but delicious. These will be one of my go-to treats!

Since other reviews said to add more milk for a less dense cupcake, I added 2 more tablespoons of milk. I also added 1/4 tsp of salt to the batter as I believe it goes there and not in the frosting, and used 2 lemons since they were small. For the frosting I used a traditional buttercream and added lemon juice and zest to that.

I doubled the recipe, but only really needed twenty cupcakes (though baked 24). Should have made 1.5x the recipe. I also used 1 tbsp of baking powder total (double recipe). I only frosted twenty cupcakes and one recipe and that was sufficient. I will add more lemon or lemon extract next time as they were not lemony enough. I also added about a 1/4 cup of applesauce to the double batch of the batter because I was making them ahead of time for a party and I feel like applesauce keeps them moist. I didn't replace the butter. Just full on added the applesauce. I thought that worked well; they were quite moist.

This recipe turned out really well. The combination of lemon and blackberry is delicious. I got 18 standard cupcakes rather than 24. Next time I would cut the baking time a little, my cupcakes could have been moister.
The buttercream went through my pastry bag perfectly, held its shape well. For my taste, it was too dense. I want to try to create a lighter version using half the butter and maybe a little cream.

I didn't think the batter had enough lemon flavor so I added the zest of one additional lemon. When done, they were still not lemony enough so I filled them with lemon curd and added an extra dollop under the buttercream. The blackberry buttercream was not great on it's on but with the tartness of the lemon curd, it worked in one bite. If I ever do a berry buttercream again, I'll remember to choose a different berry!

Delicious! Very easy to make, tasted amazing, I made mini cupcakes and this yielded more than 24 for me, and I made the frosting with a cup less of powdered sugar and it was plenty for all my cupcakes and tasted perfect.
Made these for my daughters 1st birthday!
I made this in a cake and added 1 tbls of lavender seeds and 1/4 tsp of lavender oil . everyone loved it.

Taste of summer! Just the right amount of lemon. Cupcakes were moist and flavorful. Did not have blackberry jam so I mashed some of the blackberries through a strainer. I got a very thick fruit puree which I added to the frosting which cut some of the sweetness of the frosting. Made exactly a dozen cupcakes. I would make these again!
Dry, almost burned on the bottom and raw in the middle. Shrunk down like everyone said. I didn’t try the frosting, used another recipe
Flavors compliment each other. Light, tasty cupcake

This was great. It made 24 small-ish cupcakes. The consistency was perfectly light and fluffy. I used strawberry jam instead because it's what I had on hand and used about 1/4 c more. Frosting turned out great and I don't even like bittercream. Thank you!

The recipe said to make 24 cupcakes. I wish I had filled only 18 cups. They were nicely flavored, though not strongly lemon, but a bit dry and small. The frosting, however, was delicious. Combined, they make a nice little dessert.
Tastes great, but looks horrible. The cupcakes shrunk inside their wrapper even with adding extra milk. The frosting did not go through the piping bag easily like the recipe I generally use.
Added more milk in the second batch to the cupcake batter to make them fluffier. The first ones were a bit heavy and dense. Made the icing with raspberry jam. It was fantastic!
Perfect lemon flavor! As others have stated, the yield is off, the recipe as printed will yield about 18 average size cupcakes. I did add a little blackberry extract to the icing to give it a boost.

The cupcakes turned out very dense almost like a cheesecake. Icing made too much so I had a lot left over. The jam didn’t really taste like blackberries more like grape jelly. Not much flavor to it also. Though, the lemon flavor was good! Turned out pretty in the end.

Terrific pairing. Everyone loved. I'm a kids chef. Parents can no longer bring in cupcakes for birthdays, so I do them now... and dessert grains baking is not really my forte. I simply don't do it, we don't do sweets often. So. I chose this because it was scratch, but was easy to do. Spot on for ease. And taste. However. Quantity was clearly off. I tripled this recipe to yield 48 REGULAR sized cupcakes after reading the submitter's response. It came out, by scraping the bowl. Thank you for this recipe. I will be messing with it moving forward. Cheers!!
